svg.aria-label: How to write ۰ ۱: 2 digits, ۰, ۱, one after another
svg.title: Writing ۰ ۱
svg.desc: 2 digits written one after another: ۰, ۱ (perso-arabic). Each digit has its own group of frames; frame N of a group shows movements 1 to N of that digit, the movement being added drawn in ink over the finished digit, whose outline is read from _fonts/NotoNaskhArabic-Static.ttf. Each digit is drawn at its own scale from its own cited stroke order, so the strip does not show how large the digits are next to each other, how far apart they sit, or any join between them. Stroke order: ۰: POH-Db, Persian Online Handwriting Database (SLT Lab, Amirkabir University of Technology; github.com/SLTLabAUT/POH-Db at commit 018b039, Writepads/NumberGroup; AGPL-3.0, facts only): 676 aligned samples of ۰ from 30 native writers; one stroke in 670 (99%); no settled start (the most common zone holds 120, 18%) <https://github.com/SLTLabAUT/POH-Db/tree/018b039c0f80d84da16fc9c0f7f629c746a5b3c8/Writepads/NumberGroup>; ۱: POH-Db, Persian Online Handwriting Database (SLT Lab, Amirkabir University of Technology; github.com/SLTLabAUT/POH-Db at commit 018b039, Writepads/NumberGroup; AGPL-3.0, facts only): 562 aligned samples of ۱ from 30 native writers; one stroke in 562 (100%); starts at the top left in 480 (85%) <https://github.com/SLTLabAUT/POH-Db/tree/018b039c0f80d84da16fc9c0f7f629c746a5b3c8/Writepads/NumberGroup>. Source notes on variation: ۰: Counted for this record from POH-Db's NumberGroup writepads: lines of Persian numbers that native writers wrote on FarsiHandwriting.ir with a pen, a finger or a stylus (112 writepads by 30 writers; the mouse writepads were left out), recorded as InkML, where each trace is one pen-down stroke. Each line was split into characters by horizontal overlap; of the 1,046 lines whose character count matched their label, the 1,005 whose characters ran left to right were used (which also shows that the numbers are written left to right). Zones are thirds of each character's box, and the split is heuristic, so the shares are approximate. Of 676 samples of ۰, 670 (99%) are one stroke. It is a small mark, a median 0.31 of the height of the tallest digit in its line, so a dot, not a ring. It has no settled start or direction: the most common start zone holds only 120 (18%), and 356 (53%) turn anticlockwise against 320 (47%) clockwise. The path draws a small anticlockwise ring, the majority by a few points; either direction is a dot. POH-Db is licensed AGPL-3.0, so only these counts and shares are taken; no coordinate or trace is copied, and the pen path is fitted to the bundled Noto Naskh Arabic outline rather than to any sample. Handwriting varies by writer. ۱: Counted for this record from POH-Db's NumberGroup writepads: lines of Persian numbers that native writers wrote on FarsiHandwriting.ir with a pen, a finger or a stylus (112 writepads by 30 writers; the mouse writepads were left out), recorded as InkML, where each trace is one pen-down stroke. Each line was split into characters by horizontal overlap; of the 1,046 lines whose character count matched their label, the 1,005 whose characters ran left to right were used (which also shows that the numbers are written left to right). Zones are thirds of each character's box, and the split is heuristic, so the shares are approximate. Of 562 samples of ۱, 562 (100%) are one stroke. 480 (85%) start at the top left, 508 (90%) first move down, and 489 (87%) end at the bottom right, below and to the right of the start: one slanting stroke, top to bottom. POH-Db is licensed AGPL-3.0, so only these counts and shares are taken; no coordinate or trace is copied, and the pen path is fitted to the bundled Noto Naskh Arabic outline rather than to any sample. Handwriting varies by writer.
